items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I was being assisted by John Hammond, who was giving me a lot of encouragement, helping me get the guys together... John financed my trip to Chicago

ctx.x: And after that time, I went back, you know, after leaving Fletcher while I was in this rehearsal phase of my orchestra, I was being assisted by John Hammond, who was giving me a lot of encouragement, helping me get the guys together, and then he suggested to me, well, if I really liked this pianist this well, whom he hadn't yet heard, he said, 'Why don't you try to get him?'

So I figured how could I get him out of Chicago; he was working in Chicago, and I had no money -- nobody had any money. John said, 'Well, I'll let you have the money to go after him,' you know? So John financed my trip to Chicago and I did go, drove to Chicago with a friend -- a very good friend whose name was George Ritch -- and I'll have more to say about George Ritch later because he figures kind of in my whole career a bit -- what was I talking about?
